lines.trans: Well look at that, wearing pants. These are for you.

At least I did not lie to you, I told the truth.

lines.trans: See, I have already changed. You changed?
Right. You are the exact same narcissistic egoist you always were.
Instead of simply apologizing for your stupidity.
And that is all. I agree. It was stupid.
But it was a card debt. And paying it off is a matter of honor.
Crowing without pants is not a debt, it is idiocy.
Yes, idiocy. But I promised to carry out any idiocy if I lost.
Alright then. Will you take the flowers? No.
Miss, these are for you from a man with a sense of self-respect.
Excuse me, she was bringing those flowers to me.
Give the flowers back.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agree').

examples.trans: Alright, I agree to this plan.

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оврать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lied', paired with 'врать'.

examples.text: Потому что я соврал про деньги.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'мениться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'changed', paired with 'изменяться'.

examples.text: Узнаёшь? У нас здесь ничего не изменилось.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень самовлюблённый выбор.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто самовлюблённый день в ресторане.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('own').

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стоинство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'dignity / self-respect' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он говорит, что наше главное достоинство — принципиальность.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'brought', paired with 'приносить'.
